problem: Dense retrieval systems match cross-lingual semantics well but fail systematically on queries with hard temporal constraints (named 'temporal-semantic misalignment'), and this persists after fine-tuning on temporal data, suggesting a structural rather than data-driven limitation.
method: A three-signal hybrid retrieval framework combining BM25 lexical matching, dense semantic embeddings, and exponential temporal decay; benchmark construction; evaluation of six retrieval architectures; and a fine-tuning study on 7,000+ temporal training examples.
key_assumptions: Queries carry a hard temporal constraint expressible as a target date
Temporal relevance decreases with elapsed time (exponential decay as the temporal signal)
main_contribution: A trilingual temporal retrieval benchmark (TemporalESG) and a three-signal hybrid framework showing that hard temporal constraints require explicit architectural solutions beyond representation learning.
datasets: 40,814 ESG disclosure documents from 43 multinational corporations, 11 years (2015-2025), Vietnamese/English/Arabic
baselines: Six retrieval architectures (including BM25 sparse, dense, and hybrid)
results: State-of-the-art dense retrieval reaches only 65.1% temporal accuracy; fine-tuning on 7,000+ temporal examples yields marginal recall gains while degrading top-ranked precision; the three-signal hybrid reaches 99.8% temporal accuracy and 50.8% entity precision across all three languages with cross-validated generalization.
limitations: Full text not open access; method details beyond the abstract unknown
Domain is ESG disclosure retrieval rather than amended statutes/regulations
Temporal signal is exponential decay (recency), not supersession/validity of near-duplicate successive versions
future_work: The abstract asserts the finding 'extends to any domain where temporal precision is non-negotiable, including legal, medical, and regulatory retrieval', implying legal/regulatory transfer as future work

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: This is a fixed three-signal hybrid (BM25 + dense + exponential temporal decay) evaluated on multilingual ESG disclosures, not a retrieval-agnostic temporal re-ranking term attached to an arbitrary base retriever, and it does not model supersession or validity intervals of near-duplicate successive document versions; its temporal signal equates recency with correctness. Its own framing ('extends to legal, medical, regulatory') leaves exactly the proposed legal/regulatory transfer open.
relation_to_idea.basis: Abstract explicitly describes lexical+dense+exponential-temporal-decay combination, a temporal benchmark, and temporal-accuracy metrics; the proposal's distinctive elements (retrieval-agnostic plug-in, amended statutory versions with overlapping wording) are absent from the abstract.
